explain.say: Picture a lake in Uganda with 1000 fish. Each year, every 10 fish produce about 1 extra fish. The more fish there are, the faster their number grows. Look at the first stage: 1000 fish right now.

stages.ask: Why does the solution of dP/dt = kP grow exponentially?

explain.say: Here is the key: the rate of growth depends on how many fish there are. We write dP by dt equals k times P. P is the number of fish and k is 0.1 per year. So 1000 fish grow by about 100 a year. See the second stage?

explain.say: It goes up! With 2000 fish, the rate is 200 a year. Look at the last stage: bigger amount, faster rate, and round the loop again. An equation about a rate like this is called a differential equation.

faq.a: An equation that links a quantity to its rate of change, like dP by dt equals k P. Solving it means finding the function that obeys the rule.
It means P grows at a rate proportional to P itself. Twice as much P means twice as fast growth.
asks: What does dP by dt mean?

faq.q: Why does the solution of dP/dt = kP grow exponentially?
faq.a: Growth feeds more growth: a bigger amount makes a faster rate, which makes the amount bigger still. The only function whose slope is always k times itself is P nought times e to the k t.
asks: Why is the answer e to the kt?

faq.q: How do you solve dP/dt = kP?
faq.a: Separate the variables: dP over P equals k dt. Integrate both sides to get the natural log of P equals k t plus c, so P equals P nought times e to the k t.
Then the amount shrinks, faster when it is big and slower when it is small. That is exponential decay, like a cooling drink or a medicine leaving the body.
asks: What does a negative k mean?

facts: The differential equation dP/dt = kP has solution P = P₀e^(kt).
With k = 0.1 per year, a population grows by about 10.5% each year, since e^0.1 ≈ 1.105.

quiz.say: dP by dt equals 0.2 P and P is 500. How fast is P growing right now?
quiz.show: dP/dt = 0.2P and P = 500. How fast is P growing right now?

wrong.1: 500 is the amount, not the rate.
wrong.2: 0.2 is the constant k; multiply it by P.

quiz.say: Which function solves dy by dx equals y, with y equal to 1 when x is 0?
quiz.show: Which function solves dy/dx = y with y = 1 when x = 0?
quiz.why: eˣ is its own derivative and equals 1 at x = 0.

wrong.0: The derivative of x is 1, not x.
wrong.2: The derivative of x² is 2x, not x².
